qt: to the Commission Engin Eroglu (Renew) Subject:

According to an article by Global News1, in a briefing to the Minister of Democratic Institutions on Foreign Interference the Canadian Security Intelligence Service confirmed foreign interference by the Peoples Republic of China in the 2019 and 2021 federal elections in Canada. It also emphasised that the interference took place on all levels of government and civil society. Furthermore, the article states that the briefing recommended that interference should be countered on all levels of government, including provincial and municipal governments. 1.
What kind of information does the Commission have about similar foreign interference in the EU?
What kinds of measures are in place or planned to prevent and recognise interference activities?

What kind of support does or will the Commission provide to the regions and municipalities in the EU to increase their expertise on and protect themselves against foreign interference, specifically as regards to the upcoming European Parliament elections?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.3.2024) Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) is a growing security issue that threatens the functioning of democracies and the cohesion of the European societies. The EU has been working on addressing FIMI for several years: there is a dedicated FIMI toolbox 1, which among other things puts forward a whole-society approach and sets out different instruments to tackle the threat in close cooperation among all the EU institutions, Member States, civil society, the private sector as well with international partners. Recently, the High Representative/Vice-President presented the 2nd European External Action Service (EEAS) Threat Report on FIMI2 bringing forward a collective response framework and with a specific focus on elections. This constitutes a concrete contribution to the EU’s preparedness ahead of the European elections in June 2024, which may benefit the ongoing efforts at all levels of government, including regions and municipalities in the EU. As part of its efforts to build resilience to FIMI, the EEAS devotes particular attention to cooperation with independent media and fact-checkers. The EUvsDisinfo project3 continues to raise awareness about the threat, its analysis and articles are consistently shared with EU institutions, EU delegations and international partners, translated in all EU languages, as well as Ukrainian, Georgian, Armenian, Azerbaijani, Russian, Chinese, Arabic. In addition, Horizon Europe is currently funding a portfolio of research projects4 on FIMI. With an overall budget envelope of EUR 18 million, some of the projects will engage with stakeholders outside of academia, including local government officials, to ensure that the research is relevant and responsive to the needs of regional actors.
